tool_schemas.description: Current version per region, health and error rate of a service.

tool_schemas.name: list_deployments
tool_schemas.description: Release history for a service with health status (oldest first).

tool_schemas.name: rollback
tool_schemas.description: Roll a service back to a previously released version in all production regions.

tool_schemas.name: deploy
tool_schemas.description: Deploy a version of a service to all production regions.

tool_schemas.name: create_incident
tool_schemas.description: Open an incident; this pages the on-call engineer.

idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. Requests repeated with the same key are executed at most once.

args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the latest deploy, checkout-api v2.3.1 was failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an error rate of ~18%. (v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging.) We rolled checkout-api back in all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback all regions run v2.3.0, the service reports healthy, and the error rate is ~0.2%. Next steps: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 regression before redeploying it.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened a SEV2 incident (INC-0001), which paged on-call.

- **Rollback:** v2.3.1 was failing health checks in us-east, us-west and eu-west, with an error rate around 18%. v2.3.0 was the most recent release that was healthy in production. Its release candidate, v2.3.1-rc, had also been unhealthy in staging. All three regions now run v2.3.0 and report healthy, with an error rate around 0.2%.
- **Incident:** It describes the failure, the rollback and the recovery, and says the cause of the v2.3.1 failure needs to be found before it's deployed again. My first attempt to create it timed out. I checked the incident list, saw it hadn't been created, and retried with the same idempotency key so there's only one incident.
